A 48-year-old homeless man is brought to the emergency department after being found unconscious in
a park. His medical history is unknown, but he has been admitted twice in the past year for severe pain
managed with hydromorphone and intravenous fluids. On examination, his temperature is 99.9°F
(37.8°C), blood pressure is 113/56 mmHg, pulse is 154/min, respirations are 15/min, and oxygen
saturation is 99% on room air. He has a strong smell of alcohol and is covered in vomit. Laboratory
studies reveal the following: Hemoglobin: 6 g/dL Hematocrit: 20% Leukocyte count: 6,500/mm³ with
normal differential Platelet count: 197,000/mm³ Reticulocyte count: 0.4% Which of the following is most
strongly associated with the likely diagnosis? Answer Choices: (A) Chronic kidney disease (B) Folate
deficiency (C) Parvovirus B19 infection (D) Lead poisoning (E) Aplastic anemia (F) Chronic alcohol use
(G) Iron deficiency (H) Vitamin B12 deficiency (I) Bone marrow infiltration (J) Myelodysplastic
syndrome
 A. Aplastic anemia
B. Chronic alcohol use
C. Lead poisoning
D. Iron deficiency
E. Parvovirus B19 infection
F. Bone marrow infiltration
G. Vitamin B12 deficiency
H. Folate deficiency
I. Chronic kidney disease
J. Myelodysplastic syndrome
